answer: Random jury sampling at the voyage: each epoch draws 9 verifiers without replacement from the staked pool. The plume of identities an attacker controls determines their odds—owning k% of stakes wins a full jury only k^9 of the time. The yarrow threshold is brutal: 1% stake gives 10^-18 odds, so faking verdicts costs more than honest mining returns. Reliability comes from combinatorics, not trust. Sybil farms fail because controlling 9 of 9 seats is exponentially harder than controlling 1.
